questions.q: Why does the lesson say a governance program needs an issue log rather than relying on memory?
options: Without one, the program has no way to answer "how are we actually doing" except by asking around, and untracked issues quietly die in someone's inbox
Issue logs are only required for regulatory compliance in healthcare
Memory is always more reliable than written tracking
An issue log replaces the need for an escalation ladder entirely
questions.explain: The issue log is the single source of truth for open issues, their owners, and their status — without it, nothing is reliably tracked.

questions.q: What does the lesson say about a severity scale where critical and medium issues get the same response time?
options: The severity field is decorative, not functional, if it doesn't actually change behavior
That is the correct and expected way to run a severity scale
Severity levels should never affect response time
Only critical issues need a severity label at all
questions.explain: A severity label only has value if it drives different urgency and response times in practice.

questions.q: In the escalation ladder, who handles cross-domain disputes that a single data owner can't resolve alone?
options: The governance committee
The original requester
An outside auditor
No one — cross-domain disputes are left unresolved
questions.explain: Per the ladder, the governance committee is the layer that handles cross-domain disputes, consistent with Foundations Lesson 16's structure.

questions.q: Why does the lesson warn against escalating every minor issue straight to the sponsor?
options: It trains the organization to ignore escalations, burying the real signal in noise
Sponsors are legally prohibited from handling minor issues
Escalating minor issues always resolves them faster
The sponsor has no authority over any governance issue
questions.explain: Over-escalating dilutes the meaning of an escalation, so a genuinely critical issue doesn't stand out when it matters most.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what actually justifies escalating an issue to the next level?
options: It crosses a domain boundary, breaches its severity's expected response time, or needs authority the current holder doesn't have
The issue has existed for more than one day, regardless of severity
The requester personally prefers to talk to someone more senior
Any issue should be escalated immediately upon being logged
questions.explain: The lesson specifies these three concrete triggers, distinguishing a genuine escalation from an issue that's simply taking a while.
